start.text:
D.,

I keep starting this and deleting it. You always say I'm better at writing than talking, so here.

Work has been strange. I copied something I shouldn't have. I put it where only I can open it. You laugh that I use Biscuit for every password - fine, laugh - but I added the year we met, so now it's safe. Safe from everyone except you.

If anything happens, you know what the password is. You were there.

I'll finish this tomorrow.

E.

eggs
rice
dog food (the GOOD one, he won't eat the other)
batteries
flowers for D.?

contacts backup (old phone)

mum - 0412 004 771 (disconnected)
D. - 0731 559 016
vet - 0418 220 900

MY HERO
by Lena Halden, class 3B

My hero is my uncle Pavel because he can fix anything. He fixed my bike and the radio and grandma's glasses. He says broken things just need someone to not give up on them.

He is away right now but when he comes back he is going to teach me how to fix a car.

Teacher's note: Good effort, Lena. Next time choose a hero from our national history. - Mrs. Duda

No.   NAME            FROM               BLOCK  STATUS
0371  Sorin, M.       Oster checkpoint   B      released (signed)
0388  Kolar, J.       Oster checkpoint   C      deceased
0402  Halden, P.      Oster checkpoint   C      held - no visitors - no record
0405  Mares, A.       Oster checkpoint   B      held
0406  Mares, T.       Oster checkpoint   B      held
0419  Varga, D.       Oster checkpoint   C      transferred (capital)

Authorized: Maj. R. Stanek

Note: entries marked "no record" are not to be entered in the civil registry.

If you are reading this, you bought my laptop, or they gave it to you.

I was a records clerk. I copied the ledger because a woman came to the annex every week asking about her son and every week we told her there was no record. There was a record. I typed it.

I think they know I copied it. If I'm gone, they know.

If you can, tell D. I'm sorry I never finished the letter.

- Elena
